paragraphs: We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on commercializing and developing novel treatments for gastrointestinal, or GI, diseases. Our approved products, VOQUEZNA®, VOQUEZNA® DUAL PAK® and VOQUEZNA® TRIPLE PAK®, contain vonoprazan, an oral small molecule potassium-competitive acid blocker, or PCAB. PCABs are a novel class of molecules that block acid secretion in the stomach. VOQUEZNA is the only PCAB currently approved for marketing and sale in the United States.

We began U.S. commercialization of VOQUEZNA for the treatment of erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease, or Erosive GERD, and Helicobacter pylori, or H. pylori, infection, and VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK for the treatment of H. pylori infection, in November 2023. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, approved VOQUEZNA for the relief of heartburn associated with Non-Erosive GERD, the largest category of GERD, in July 2024.

Vonoprazan was originally developed by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited, or Takeda, and is marketed in multiple countries outside the United States. We licensed U.S., European and Canadian rights to vonoprazan from Takeda in 2019. We are independently commercializing VOQUEZNA, VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK in the United States.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated increased revenues from sales of our VOQUEZNA products compared to the prior year, reflecting continued execution of our U.S. commercial strategy. The majority of our 2025 revenue was derived from sales of VOQUEZNA. During this period, we also experienced growth in prescription volume and prescriber adoption, with most prescriptions written for GERD indications. As of February 13, 2026, over 1.1 million prescriptions for VOQUEZNA, VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK have been filled since launch. We continue to have broad commercial coverage for VOQUEZNA, with access for over 120 million, or over 80%, of U.S. commercial lives. Our commercial efforts are supported by a targeted sales force and continued focus on prescriber engagement and payer access.

In May 2021, the FDA granted qualified infectious disease product, or QIDP, designation to VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK, resulting in an extension of the five-year new chemical entity, or NCE, exclusivity by an additional five years. In December 2024, we submitted a citizen petition requesting that the FDA update the Orange Book listing for VOQUEZNA to reflect the same ten-year period of NCE exclusivity applicable to VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK. In June 2025, the FDA granted the petition and updated the Orange Book listing for VOQUEZNA to reflect the ten-year period of NCE exclusivity for vonoprazan. As a result, all three VOQUEZNA products now have NCE exclusivity extending through May 3, 2032.

In the fourth quarter of 2025, we initiated a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vonoprazan in the treatment of adults with eosinophilic esophagitis, or EoE. While our current focus is on continued U.S. commercialization of VOQUEZNA products for GERD and H. pylori, we are also evaluating other potential life-cycle management opportunities for vonoprazan. We may also explore the potential for vonoprazan in Europe and Canada, as well as opportunities to in-license or acquire additional clinical or commercial-stage product candidates for GI diseases.

All of our revenue is derived from the sale of three products in the United States: VOQUEZNA (vonoprazan) tablets which are approved for the healing and maintenance of healing of all grades of Erosive GERD and relief of heartburn associated with Erosive GERD in adults, and for the relief of heartburn associated with Non-Erosive GERD in adults, as well as, in combination with amoxicillin with or without clarithromycin, for the treatment of H. pylori infection, and VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK, comprised of vonoprazan co-packaged with amoxicillin, and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK, comprised of vonoprazan co-packaged with amoxicillin and clarithromycin, which are both approved for the treatment of H. pylori infection. We began U.S. commercialization of VOQUEZNA for the treatment of Erosive GERD and H. pylori infection, and of VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK for the treatment of H. pylori infection, in the fourth quarter of 2023. In July 2024, the FDA also approved VOQUEZNA for the relief of heartburn associated with Non-Erosive GERD.
The sections below describe the diseases our approved products target, the clinical data supporting their use, and our commercialization efforts.
Our strategy is focused on building a sustainable, commercial-stage GI company centered on the commercialization of VOQUEZNA and, in the future, the disciplined expansion of our product portfolio.

• Maximizing the U.S. commercial opportunity for VOQUEZNA in its approved indications in the treatment of GERD through a targeted sales force initially focused on gastroenterologists and other high-prescribing healthcare providers, and in the future, potentially expanding marketing and sales efforts to target more broadly those primary care physicians who treat GERD;
• Selectively pursuing life-cycle management opportunities for vonoprazan, including potential additional indications and formulations;

• Exploring the potential for vonoprazan in Europe, Canada, U.S. over-the counter, or OTC, use, and other potential market expansions, including evaluating the feasibility and practicality of potential collaboration or licensing arrangements;

• Maintaining a disciplined and selective approach to business development, including evaluating opportunities to in-license or acquire additional clinical- or commercial-stage product candidates for GI diseases; and
• Operating with financial discipline, prioritizing efficient capital allocation and effective management of manufacturing and supply arrangements.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Position and Capital Requirements
We have a limited operating history as a commercial company, which may make it difficult to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability.
We have incurred significant operating losses since inception and may never achieve or maintain profitability.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or product candidates.
Risks Related to Commercialization of VOQUEZNA, VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK, VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK and Any Future Product Candidates

Our future growth may depend, in part, on our ability to operate in foreign markets, particularly Europe and Canada, where we would be subject to additional regulatory burdens and other risks and uncertainties.
Risks Related to the Development and Regulatory Approval of Product Candidates
Our future growth depends on our ability to develop vonoprazan for additional indications or formulations and to successfully develop or acquire additional product candidates.

Clinical development is lengthy, expensive and uncertain, and delays or failures in our clinical trials could limit our ability to obtain additional regulatory approvals and adversely affect our business.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors, together with the other information contained in this annual report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," before making a decision to purchase or sell shares of our common stock. We cannot assure you that any of the events discussed in the risk factors below will not occur. These risks could have a material and adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and growth prospects. If that were to happen, the trading price of our common stock could decline. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations or financial condition. In this section, we first provide a summary of the more principal risks and uncertainties we face and then provide a full set of risk factors and discuss them in greater detail.

• We have a limited operating history, have incurred significant operating losses since our inception and may never become profitable or, if we achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain it;

• We currently depend entirely on the success of our approved VOQUEZNA products, and in particular on the success of VOQUEZNA for the treatment of GERD. If we are unable to successfully commercialize VOQUEZNA at the levels we expect, our business, results of operations, and prospects will be materially harmed;

• We may require additional financing to achieve our goals, finance our operations and meet our financial obligations, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our commercialization activities, product development programs, or other operations;

• Our Revenue Interest Financing Agreement could limit cash flow available for our operations and expose us to risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations;

• In the future we will need to successfully acquire, develop and gain approval of one or more product candidates other than VOQUEZNA with significant market potential. If we are not successful in these efforts, our business prospects may be materially and adversely affected;

We commenced our operations in 2018 and have devoted substantially all of our resources to date to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, in-licensing vonoprazan, meeting with regulatory authorities, managing our clinical trials of vonoprazan, preparing for commercialization of our products containing vonoprazan, commercially launching our approved products in the U.S., and providing other selling, general and administrative support for our operations. Our operations to date have been funded primarily through commercial bank debt, our revenue interest financing debt and various equity offerings, including our at-the-market offerings. From our inception through December 31, 2025, we sold 34,737,032 shares of our common stock and 2,608,922 pre-funded warrants, generating net proceeds of approximately $543.3 million, after deducting underwriting discounts, commissions and offering costs. In January 2026, we sold 6,875,000 shares of our common stock, or our January 2026 Offering, at a price of $16.00 per share and pre-funded warrants to purchase 1,250,078 shares of our common stock at a price of $15.999 per pre-funded warrant for total gross proceeds of $130.0 million or $122.2 million of net proceeds after deducting underwriting discounts, commissions and offering costs.

As of December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $130.0 million. Based on our current operating plan, we believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents together with anticipated product revenues and the $122.2 million of net proceeds from our January 2026 offering, are sufficient to fund operations for at least the next twelve months and will be sufficient to enable us to reach operating profitability beginning in the third quarter of 2026, excluding stock-based compensation. We have based these estimates on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we could use our capital resources sooner than we currently expect. Our operating plans and other demands on our cash resources may change as a result of many factors currently unknown to us, and we may need to seek additional funds sooner than planned, through public or private equity or debt financings or other capital sources, including potentially collaborations, licenses and other similar arrangements. In addition, we may seek additional capital due to favorable market conditions or strategic considerations even if we believe we have sufficient funds for our current or future operating plans. Attempting to secure additional financing may divert our management from our day-to-day activities, which may adversely affect our ability to commercialize VOQUEZNA, develop vonoprazan for additional indications or formulations or develop or any future product candidates.

Since inception, we have incurred significant operating losses. Our net loss was $221.2 million and $334.3 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.5 billion. Despite our plans and expectations, we could continue to incur operating losses for the foreseeable future. If we do not achieve our goals, it could be several years, if ever, before our current products or potential future product candidates, if successfully developed and approved, generate significant revenues to offset these operating losses. As a result, we are uncertain if we will achieve profitability on our current expected timeline, if at all, and, if so, whether we will be able to sustain it. The net losses we incur may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and year to year.

While we have generated revenue to date, until such time as we can generate significant revenue from sales of our approved products containing vonoprazan, we also expect to finance our cash needs through equity offerings, additional debt financings or other capital sources, including potential collaborations, licenses and other similar arrangements. However, we may be unable to raise additional funds or enter into such other arrangements when and if needed on favorable terms or at all, and this risk could be exacerbated by the impact of ongoing conflicts throughout the world and global economic conditions. Our failure to raise capital or enter into such other arrangements when needed would have a negative impact on our financial condition and could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development or future commercialization efforts or grant rights to develop and market product candidates that we would otherwise prefer to develop and market ourselves.

In May 2025, we implemented a cost reduction and organizational restructuring plan to reduce cash burn and focus resources on commercial execution. In connection with the restructuring, our workforce was reduced by 26 employees, or approximately 6%, including certain leadership changes all designed to right-size the organization. During the year ended December 31, 2025, total restructuring charges incurred were $9.2 million consisting of one-time termination benefits to affected employees for severance, non-cash stock-based compensation costs, healthcare benefits and outplacement assistance. As of December 31, 2025, approximately $0.5 million of restructuring related accruals remain on our balance sheet.

On May 7, 2019, we and Takeda entered into an exclusive license, or the Takeda License, pursuant to which we in-licensed the U.S., European, and Canadian rights to vonoprazan fumarate. During the term of the Takeda License, we and our affiliates are not permitted to commercialize any pharmaceutical product, other than vonoprazan, that treats acid-related disorders, except for certain generic and OTC competing products in specified circumstances. We are responsible at our cost for the development, manufacture and commercialization of vonoprazan products. We are required to use commercially reasonable efforts to develop and commercialize the vonoprazan products in our licensed territory.

Under the Takeda License, Takeda has the sole right and authority, with our input, to prepare, file, prosecute, and maintain all Takeda and joint patents on a worldwide basis at its own cost. We are responsible, at our cost, for preparing, filing, prosecuting, and maintaining patents on inventions made solely by us in connection with vonoprazan, subject to input from Takeda.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，專注於商業化與開發用以治療消化道，或稱 GI，疾病的創新治療方式。本公司已核准產品 VOQUEZNA®、VOQUEZNA® DUAL PAK® 與 VOQUEZNA® TRIPLE PAK® 含有 vonoprazan，一種口服小分子鉀競爭性酸阻斷劑，或稱 PCAB。PCAB 是一種新興的分子類別，可阻斷胃酸分泌。VOQUEZNA 是目前唯一獲美國核准上市與銷售的 PCAB。

我們於 2023 年 11 月開始美國 VOQUEZNA 的商業化，用以治療潰瘍性胃食道逆流，或稱 Erosive GERD，以及幽門螺旋桿菌，或稱 H. pylori，感染，以及 VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK 與 VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK 用以治療 H. pylori 感染。美國食品藥物管理局，或稱 FDA，於 2024 年 7 月核准 VOQUEZNA 用以緩解非潰瘍性胃食道逆流，即為 GERD 中最大類別，所引起的胃灼熱症狀。
Vonoprazan 最初是由 Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited，或稱 Takeda，所開發，並在美國以外的多個國家進行市場推廣。我們於 2019 年自 Takeda 獲得美國、歐洲與加拿大 vonoprazan 的權利。我們獨立於美國進行 VOQUEZNA、VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK 與 VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK 的商業化。

於2025年12月31日財務年度，我們來自VOQUEZNA產品銷售的營業收入較前一年增加，反映我們美國商業策略持續有效執行。2025年我們的大部分營業收入來自VOQUEZNA產品銷售。於此期間，我們也觀察到處方量與處方醫師採用率成長，其中大多數處方為GERD適應症。截至2026年2月13日，自產品上市以來，VOQUEZNA、VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK及VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK已累計填發超過1.1百萬張處方。我們持續擁有廣泛的VOQUEZNA商業 coverage，可提供超過120百萬，或超過80%，的美國商業保險人口使用。我們的商業努力由針對性的銷售團隊支持，並持續著重於處方醫師參與及保險給付方的准入。

2021 年 5 月，美國食品藥物管理局，或稱 FDA，授予 VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK 與 VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK 合格傳染病產品，或稱 QIDP，資格，使五年的新化學實體，或稱 NCE，獨佔期延長五年。2024 年 12 月，我們提交一項公民請願書，請求 FDA 更新 VOQUEZNA 的橙皮書登錄，以反映與 VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK 與 VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK 相同的十年 NCE 獨佔期。2025 年 6 月，FDA 授予請願書，並更新 VOQUEZNA 的橙皮書登錄，以反映 vonoprazan 的十年 NCE 獨佔期。因此，所有三種 VOQUEZNA 產品現在的 NCE 獨佔期延長至 2032 年 5 月 3 日。

在 2025 年第四季，我們啟動一項第二期臨牀試驗，評估 vonoprazan 在治療成人嗜酸性食道炎，或稱 EoE 的應用。雖然我們目前的重點是持續美國 VOQUEZNA 產品的商業化，用以治療 GERD 與 H. pylori，我們也在評估 vonoprazan 的其他潛在生命週期管理機會。我們也可能探討 vonoprazan 在歐洲與加拿大應用的潛力，以及取得或收購其他臨牀或商業階段的 GI 疾病產品候選藥物的機會。

我們所有的收入均來自美國銷售的三種產品：VOQUEZNA（vonoprazan）片劑，核准用以治療所有等級的潰瘍性胃食道逆流，並維持其癒合，以及緩解與潰瘍性胃食道逆流相關的胃灼熱症狀，適用於成人，以及緩解與非潰瘍性胃食道逆流相關的胃灼熱症狀，適用於成人，並與阿莫西林搭配使用，或與阿莫西林與克拉維酸鉀搭配使用，用以治療 H. pylori 感染；VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK，由 vonoprazan 與阿莫西林組合包裝而成；VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK，由 vonoprazan 與阿莫西林與克拉維酸鉀組合包裝而成，均核准用以治療 H. pylori 感染。我們於 2023 年第四季開始美國 VOQUEZNA 的商業化，用以治療 Erosive GERD 與 H. pylori 感染，以及 VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK 與 VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK 用以治療 H. pylori 感染。2024 年 7 月，FDA 也核准 VOQUEZNA 用以緩解與非潰瘍性胃食道逆流相關的胃灼熱症狀。
以下段落說明我們核准產品所針對的疾病、支持其使用的臨牀數據，以及我們的商業化努力。
本公司策略聚焦於建立一個可持續發展、具商業規模的消化道疾病（GI）公司，以VOQUEZNA的商業化為中心，並在未來以嚴謹的方式擴充產品組合。
• 透過針對性的銷售團隊，最初專注於胃腸科醫師及其他處方率高的醫療專業人員，以最大化VOQUEZNA在美國核准適應症用於治療胃食道逆流症（GERD）的商業機會；未來潛在擴展市場與銷售努力，以更廣泛地針對治療胃食道逆流症的門診醫師。
• 選擇性地追求vonoprazan的產品生命週期管理機會，包括潛在的其他適應症與劑型。
• 探索vonoprazan在歐洲、加拿大、美國非處方藥（OTC）使用或其他潛在市場擴張的可能性，包括評估潛在合作或授權安排的可行性與實務性；
• 保持嚴謹且選擇性的企業發展策略，包括評估取得或授權其他臨牀或商業階段的消化道疾病產品候選藥物的機會；以及
• 以財務紀律運作，優先考量資金的有效配置，並有效管理製造與供應鏈安排。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之分析，並與本年度財務報表及其附註說明一併參考。此分析與討論包含基於我們目前信念、計畫與預期之向前看陳述，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性與假設。我們實際結果可能與這些向前看陳述所預期的有重大差異，原因包括那些於「風險因素」或本年度財務報告其他部分所列舉之因素。
我們是一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，專注於商業化與開發用於胃腸道，或GI，疾病的創新治療方式。我們核准上市的產品VOQUEZNA®、VOQUEZNA® DUAL PAK®與VOQUEZNA® TRIPLE PAK®含有vonoprazan，一種口服小分子鉀競爭性酸阻斷劑，或PCAB。PCAB是一種新興的分子類別，可阻斷胃部酸分泌。VOQUEZNA是目前唯一核准在美國上市與銷售的PCAB。

我們於2023年11月開始美國市場的VOQUEZNA商業化，用於治療糜爛性胃食道逆流症，或Erosive GERD，以及Helicobacter pylori，或H. pylori，感染，以及VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK與VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK用於治療H. pylori感染。美國食品藥物管理局，或FDA，於2024年7月核准VOQUEZNA用於緩解非糜爛性胃食道逆流症，即GERD最大類別，所引起的胸痛。
Vonoprazan最初由Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited，或Takeda，開發，並在美國以外的多個國家進行市場推廣。我們於2019年從Takeda取得美國、歐洲與加拿大市場的權利。我們獨立於美國市場商業化VOQUEZNA、VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK與VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK。

在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度，我們來自VOQUEZNA產品銷售的收入較前一年增加，反映我們持續執行美國市場商業策略。2025年我們的收入主要來自VOQUEZNA的銷售。在這個期間，我們也經歷處方量與開處醫師採用率的成長，大多數處方為GERD適應症。截至2026年2月13日，自上市以來，VOQUEZNA、VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK與VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK已填發超過1.1百萬張處方。我們持續擁有廣泛的商業覆蓋，VOQUEZNA可提供超過120百萬，或超過80%，的美國商業保險人口使用。我們的商業努力受到針對性的銷售團隊支持，並持續著重於開處醫師參與與保險商准入。

2021年5月，FDA授予VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK與VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK合格傳染病產品，或QIDP，資格，使五年的新化學實體，或NCE，獨佔期延長五年。2024年12月，我們提交公民請願書，請求FDA更新VOQUEZNA的橙皮書登錄，以反映與VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK與VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK相同的十年NCE獨佔期。2025年6月，FDA批准請願書，並更新VOQUEZNA的橙皮書登錄，以反映vonoprazan的十年NCE獨佔期。因此，所有三種VOQUEZNA產品現在的NCE獨佔期延長至2032年5月3日。
在2025年第四季，我們啟動一項第二期臨牀試驗，評估vonoprazan在治療成人嗜酸性食道炎，或EoE，的應用。雖然我們目前的重點是持續於美國市場商業化VOQUEZNA產品用於GERD與H. pylori，我們也選擇性地追求vonoprazan的產品生命週期管理機會。我們也可能探討vonoprazan在歐洲與加拿大之潛力，以及取得或收購其他臨牀或商業階段的GI疾病產品候選品之機會。

我們於2018年開始營運，至今我們將幾乎所有資源投入於組織與僱用公司、商業計畫、籌資、取得vonoprazan的授權、與監管機構會談、管理vonoprazan的臨牀試驗、準備含有vonoprazan產品的商業化、於美國市場核准產品的商業發行，以及提供其他營銷、一般與行政支持。至今我們的營運主要透過商業銀行貸款、我們的收入利息融資貸款與多種股票發行，包括我們的場內發行來資金。從我們成立至2025年12月31日，我們發行34,737,032股普通股與2,608,922張預先資金權證，產生約543.3百萬美元淨資金，扣除經紀折扣、佣金與發行費用後。2026年1月，我們發行6,875,000股普通股，或我們的2026年1月發行，每股16.00美元，並發行預先資金權證購入1,250,078股普通股，每股15.999美元，總共產生130.0百萬美元的毛資金，扣除經紀折扣、佣金與發行費用後為122.2百萬美元淨資金。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司持有現金及現金等價物為 130.0 百萬美元。根據我們目前的營運計畫，我們認為現有現金及現金等價物，加上預期產品收入，以及 2026 年 1 月發行所預期的 122.2 百萬美元淨資金，足夠支應至少未來十二個月的營運資金，並足以使我們在 2026 年第三季開始達成營運獲利，不計股票基於報酬。我們所依據的這些估計是基於可能錯誤的假設，我們可能比目前預期的時間更早使用這些資金。我們的營運計畫及其他對現金資源的需求，可能因許多目前未知的因素而改變，我們可能需要比預期更早尋求額外資金，透過公開或私人股權或債務融資或其他資金來源，包括潛在的合作、授權及其他類似安排。此外，我們可能因市場條件有利或戰略考量而尋求額外資金，即使我們認為目前或未來的營運計畫有足夠資金。試圖取得額外融資可能使我們的管理層分心於日常業務，這可能會不利於我們商業化 VOQUEZNA、開發 vonoprazan 用於其他適應症或製劑，或開發任何未來的產品候選物。

自成立以來，本公司已產生重大營運虧損。本公司淨虧損為221.2 百萬美元及334.3 百萬美元，分別為2025年及2024年12月31日結帳年度的數字。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累積虧損為1.5 十億美元。儘管本公司計畫與預期，本公司可能在可預見的未來持續產生營運虧損。如果本公司未能達成目標，可能需要數年，甚至永遠，才能使目前產品或潛在未來產品候選物，若成功開發並獲批准，產生足夠收入來彌補這些營運虧損。因此，本公司不確定是否能在預期時間內達成獲利，或是否能維持獲利。本公司產生的淨虧損可能在季度與年度之間大幅波動。

雖然本公司迄今已產生收入，但在本公司能透過銷售含vonoprazan的核准產品產生顯著收入之前，本公司也預期透過股權發行、額外債務融資或其他資金來源，包括潛在的合作、授權及其他類似安排，來籌措現金需求。然而，本公司可能無法在需要時以有利條件或完全無法取得額外資金或進入這些其他安排，此風險可能因全球衝突持續進行及全球經濟條件的影響而更加嚴重。本公司若無法在需要時取得資金或進入這些其他安排，將對財務狀況產生負面影響，並可能迫使本公司延遲、限制、減少或終止產品開發或未來商業化努力，或讓與開發與行銷產品候選物的權利，而本公司原本較傾向自行開發與行銷。

2025年5月，本公司實施了一項成本削減與組織重整計畫，以減少現金消耗並聚焦於商業執行。配合重整，本公司員工數減少26人，約為總人數的6%，包括某些領導層變動，皆旨在調整組織規模。截至2025年12月31日結帳年度，總計重整費用為9.2 百萬美元，包含對受影響員工的一次性離職補償、非現金股票基於報酬成本、醫療保險福利及職務轉移協助。截至2025年12月31日，約有0.5 百萬美元的重整相關應計餘額留存於資產負債表中。

2019年5月7日，本公司與Takeda簽訂了一項獨家授權，或稱為Takeda授權，根據該授權，本公司取得vonoprazan fumarate的美國、歐洲及加拿大權利。在Takeda授權期間，本公司及其附屬公司不得商業化任何治療酸相關疾病的藥物產品，除了vonoprazan，除外某些通用藥與非處方藥競爭產品在特定情況下。本公司負擔成本，負責vonoprazan產品的開發、製造與商業化。本公司有義務以商業上合理的努力，在授權範圍內開發與商業化vonoprazan產品。
根據Takeda授權，Takeda有權在本公司意見下，自行負擔成本，準備、提交、爭取及維護所有Takeda及共同專利於全球範圍內。本公司負擔成本，準備、提交、爭取及維護專利於本公司所開發的vonoprazan相關發明，但需考慮Takeda的意見。

headings: 與本公司有限經營歷史、財務狀況及資金需求相關之風險
本公司作為商業公司之經營歷史有限，可能使評估本公司迄今業務之成功程度及評估本公司未來生存能力變得困難。
自設立以來，本公司已產生重大營運虧損，可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋、限制本公司營運或要求本公司放棄對智慧財產權或產品候選藥物之權利。
與VOQUEZNA、VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK、VOQUEZNA DUAL PAK及任何未來產品候選藥物之商業化相關之風險
本公司未來成長可能部分取決於本公司在海外市場之經營能力，特別是歐洲及加拿大，而在這些地區本公司將面臨額外之監管負擔及其他風險與不確定性。
與產品候選藥物之開發及監管核准相關之風險
本公司未來成長取決於本公司開發vonoprazan用以治療其他適應症或製劑之能力，以及成功開發或取得其他產品候選藥物之能力。

paragraphs: 您應謹慎考量下列風險因素，並配合本年度10-K表報表中其他資訊，包括財務報表及相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，以作為是否買進或賣出本公司普通股之決策依據。本公司無法保證下列風險因素中所提及之事件不會發生。這些風險可能對本公司之業務、營運成果、財務狀況與成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。若發生此種情況，本公司普通股之交易價格可能下跌。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或本公司認為不重要，也可能影響本公司之業務營運或財務狀況。在本節中，我們首先提供一個關於我們所面臨之較重要風險與不確定性之總結，然後提供完整的風險因素清單並詳細討論。
• 本公司之營運歷史有限，自成立以來已產生顯著之營運虧損，可能永遠無法實現盈利，或即使實現盈利，也可能無法維持盈利；
• 本公司目前完全依賴已核准之VOQUEZNA產品之成功，特別是VOQUEZNA用於治療GERD之成功。若本公司無法在預期之層面成功商業化VOQUEZNA，將對本公司之業務、營運成果與前景造成重大損害；

• 未來本公司將需要成功取得、開發並獲得批准之產品候選物（除VOQUEZNA外）之一或多項，這些產品具有重大市場潛力。若本公司未能在這些努力中取得成功，將可能對本公司之業務前景造成重大且不利的影響；
